meta.purpose: calibration on the certified layer A records: one table per test target, never a single reject-rate column
meta.grid_rebuild_note: the layer A grid is read from step 3 by cell key; rebuilding it here would let the two drift apart without any check failing
meta.seed_note: one independent stream per table, so adding a table later cannot shift an earlier table's draws
meta.test: two-sided Wald on the log odds ratio, critical value from the error function rather than a hard-coded 1.96

I_type_I_error.definition: or_true = 1 and delta = 0; the population observed OR is exactly 1, so every rejection is an error

D_detection_rate.definition: or_true < 1 and delta > 0; the null is false, so a rejection is a detection and not a type I error

P_power_at_no_asymmetry.definition: or_true < 1 and delta = 0; the reference ceiling for table D, named power because there is no asymmetry

checks.question: in the or_true = 1, delta = 0 cells, does the two-sided Wald test reject at the nominal 5 per cent?
checks.rule: a cell passes when |rate - alpha| <= max(3 MC standard errors, 2 pp); the pooled rate must be within max(3 MC SE, 0.5 pp)

checks.question: at delta = delta_tip, is the population observed OR exactly 1 AND the rejection rate materially above zero?
checks.why_this_matters: a rejection rate of about zero at delta_tip would mean the population OR had been confused with the sample OR; the rate must sit near alpha, because at delta_tip the null of no observed difference is exactly true

checks.question: pooled over cells, does the detection rate fall as delta approaches delta_tip?
checks.note: at the last fraction the population observed OR is 1, so the rate there is expected to sit near alpha rather than near zero

checks.question: are the type I, detection and power tables separately and uniquely named, so that no reader or later edit can collapse them into one reject-rate column?
checks.key_scan_excludes: the type I table itself, whose name is the one the rule forbids elsewhere
checks.rule: each table declares exactly one metric name; every record repeats only that name; no field of the detection or power table may be named type_i; the three names must be pairwise distinct
checks.why_this_check_exists: the conflation of the two targets is not a wording problem, it is a wrong denominator attached to a wrong hypothesis. Structural uniqueness survives later edits in a way that a prose reminder does not, and the prose itself must stay allowed to state the distinction

checks.question: is usable_reps recorded per cell, is any cell left with too few replicates to summarise, and was the zero-cell drop rule ever actually reached?
checks.rule: a cell with usable_reps below half the requested count is reported as infeasible rather than summarised
checks.honesty_note: the drop rule did not bind on this grid: zero cells never occurred, so this check certifies only that every cell kept a full set of usable replicates. Deleting the drop rule outright does not change any number here. The rule is retained because n = 100 with an extreme risk would reach it, and because an unrecorded drop is exactly the failure the sampling rule forbids

checks.question: does the zero-cell drop rule actually fire when it should, and is the rate computed on the survivors?
checks.why_separate_from_the_accounting_check: the grid in this step never produces a zero cell, so the accounting check cannot exercise the rule. This probe can, and fails if the rule stops working
